And what they program for you is still in common programming languages- a site built with claude code isn't using a Claude programming language. It's still using HTML and CSS and so on. Fundamentally, these systems end up being AI brand agnostic.

top_comments.author: @tembeikingsleytembei
top_comments.text:
This is a timestamp for the 6 levels:

Level 1: The Amateur (0:23 - 1:19): Treating Claude like a simple search engine rather than a powerful tool. 
Level 2: The Regular (1:21 - 4:18): Utilizing Projects to create a persistent workspace with specific context, master prompts, and organizational files.
Level 3: The Integrator (4:23 - 6:42): Connecting Claude to external tools like Gmail, Calendar, Drive, and Slack to streamline workflows.
Level 4: The Operator (6:43 - 9:34): Moving from doer to director by using system prompts, saving skills, and scheduling tasks with automation tools like co-work.
Level 5: The Builder (9:35 - 12:12): Using Claude Code to write software, build internal tools, and create custom apps using natural language.
Level 6: The Agent Orchestrator (12:13 - 14:10): Designing an agent system with a main orchestrator and specialized sub-agents to execute entire workflows autonomously.
